revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Evidence Locker
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Chen logs evidence bags into the agency vault. After she adds 18 new bags from today's case, the vault holds 64 bags in all. The equation b + 18 = 64 shows the situation, where b is the number of bags that were already in the vault. How many evidence bags were in the vault before today?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Subtract 18 from both sides: b = 64 − 18 = 46. There were 46 evidence bags in the vault before today. Check: 46 + 18 = 64 ✓

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do I solve an addition or subtraction equation?
conceptIntro.intro: To solve means to find the value that makes the equation true. I use the inverse operation (the opposite) to get the variable alone, and I do the same thing to both sides. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Undo the operation with its inverse, and do it to both sides to keep the equation balanced.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Solve n + 23 = 58. The 23 is added to n.
The inverse of adding 23 is subtracting 23.
I subtract 23 from both sides: n + 23 − 23 = 58 − 23.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Solve x − 4 = 9. Is x being added or subtracted?
It is subtracted, so the inverse is adding 4 to both sides.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "To undo the operation I ___ both sides, and the solution is ___ ."

youDo.title: Now you try — with support
lines: Use the balance scale to solve n + 19 = 46 — a new equation, not the n + 23 = 58 we just watched.
Then solve the practice equations and check each answer.

explore.instructions: Use the balance scale to solve n + 19 = 46. What must you do to both sides to isolate n?
hints: To isolate n, you need to remove the +19. What is the inverse of adding 19?
Subtract 19 from BOTH sides: n + 19 − 19 = 46 − 19 → n = 27.
explore.label: Solve the equation using the balance scale. Keep both sides equal!

discourse.prompt: Why do you have to subtract 19 from BOTH sides, not just one?
discourse.sentenceFrame: I subtract from both sides because an equation is like a ___ — to keep it balanced, any operation on one side must ___.

diagram.intro: Now write the solving steps on paper-style lines — I'll check each one keeps the same solution.

approaching.explanation: Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9 = 6. Check: 6 + 9 = 15 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9 = ___.
That number is already showing in the equation as the amount being added, not the unknown. Undo the addition by subtracting it from both sides.
That is the total after 9 was added, not the starting value. Work backward from the total by subtracting 9 from both sides.
hints: x has 9 added to it. To get x alone, you need to UNDO that addition.
Use the inverse operation: subtraction undoes addition. Whatever you do, do it to BOTH sides to keep the balance.
Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9. Then check by adding 9 back to your result — do you land on 15?
approaching.explanationEs: Resta 9 en ambos lados: x = 15 − 9 = 6. Comprueba: 6 + 9 = 15 ✓

approaching.explanation: Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7 = 27. Check: 27 − 7 = 20 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7 = ___.
That is the amount being subtracted, not the value of y. Undo the subtraction by adding it to both sides.
The two numbers got multiplied. Subtraction is undone by addition, so add 7 to both sides instead.
hints: Look at what's happening to y: 7 is being SUBTRACTED. Which operation undoes subtraction?
Add the same amount to both sides so the equation stays balanced and y ends up alone.
Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7. Check your result: does it minus 7 give back 20?
approaching.explanationEs: Suma 7 en ambos lados: y = 20 + 7 = 27. Comprueba: 27 − 7 = 20 ✓

approaching.explanation: Subtract 15 from both sides: n = 42 − 15 = 27. Check: 27 + 15 = 42 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 15 from both sides: n = 42 − 15 = ___.
That is the amount being added, not the starting value. Subtract 15 from both sides to peel it away from n.
That is the total after 15 was added. Work backward from the total by subtracting 15 from both sides.
hints: n is being increased by 15. To find n alone, you must undo that addition.
Subtract 15 from both sides — the +15 and −15 cancel on the left, leaving just n.
Compute 42 − 15 carefully (42 − 10 = 32, then take away 5 more). Check by adding 15 back to your answer.
approaching.explanationEs: Resta 15 en ambos lados: n = 42 − 15 = 27. Comprueba: 27 + 15 = 42 ✓

approaching.explanation: Add 11 to both sides: m = 25 + 11 = 36. Check: 36 − 11 = 25 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Add 11 to both sides: m = 25 + 11 = ___.
That is the result after 11 was taken away, not the starting value. Add 11 to both sides to get back to m.
The two numbers got multiplied. Subtraction is undone by addition, so add 11 to both sides instead.
hints: m has 11 taken away from it. Think about which operation puts that 11 back.
Addition undoes subtraction: add 11 to both sides to leave m by itself.
Compute 25 + 11 for m. Then check: your answer minus 11 should equal 25.
approaching.explanationEs: Suma 11 en ambos lados: m = 25 + 11 = 36. Comprueba: 36 − 11 = 25 ✓

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: You must subtract 6 from BOTH sides, not just the left. x + 6 − 6 = 14 − 6, so x = 8. Check: 8 + 6 = 14 ✓
hints: Step 3 only subtracted 6 from the left side. What happened to the right side?
To keep the equation balanced, subtract 6 from both sides: 14 − 6 = 8, so x = 8.
approaching.explanation: The inverse operation chosen was right, but the "Subtract from one side only" step applies it to the left side alone. Whatever you do to one side of an equation must happen to the other, so subtract 6 from both: x + 6 − 6 = 14 − 6 gives x = 8. Checking, 8 + 6 = 14, while the student's x = 14 would make the left side 20.
approaching.explanationEs: La operación inversa elegida fue correcta, pero el paso "Subtract from one side only" la aplica solo al lado izquierdo. Lo que le haces a un lado de una ecuación se lo debes hacer al otro, así que resta 6 en ambos: x + 6 − 6 = 14 − 6 da x = 8. Al comprobar, 8 + 6 = 14, mientras que el x = 14 del estudiante haría que el lado izquierdo fuera 20.

approaching.stem: A shirt costs $d. After a $15 discount, it costs $38. What is d?
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you subtracted 15 from 38. Instead: d − 15 = 38 → d = 38 + 15 = $53.
That is the price after the discount, not the original price. The original price has to be larger, so add the discount back on.
The discount was not added back fully. Set up d − 15 = 38, then add 15 to both sides and combine carefully.
hints: The $15 discount was taken OFF the original price d, and $38 is what's left after the discount.
Write the story first: d − 15 = 38. Then undo the subtraction — the original price should be MORE than $38, not less.
Add the $15 discount back onto the $38 sale price: d = 38 + 15. Which choice matches that total?
approaching.stemEs: Una camisa cuesta $d. Después de un descuento de $15, cuesta $38. ¿Cuánto vale d?

onLevel.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides: x = 15 − 7 = 8. Check: 8 + 7 = 15 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 7 from both sides: x = 15 − 7 = ___.
That is the number being added in the equation, not the unknown value. Subtract it from both sides to uncover x.
The two numbers got multiplied. Addition is undone by subtraction, so take 7 away from both sides instead.
onLevel.explanationEs: Resta 7 en ambos lados: x = 15 − 7 = 8. Comprueba: 8 + 7 = 15 ✓
hints: The equation shows something being added to x, and the equal sign means both sides have the same value.
Use the inverse operation: whatever is added to x should be subtracted from both sides.
Subtract 7 from both sides. The left side becomes just x, and the right side becomes 15 − 7 — finish that subtraction.
hintsEs: La ecuación muestra que algo se le suma a x, y el signo igual significa que ambos lados tienen el mismo valor.
Usa la operación inversa: lo que se le suma a x debe restarse en ambos lados.
Resta 7 en ambos lados. El lado izquierdo queda solo como x y el derecho queda como 15 − 7 — termina esa resta.

onLevel.explanation: Add 4 to both sides: n = 9 + 4 = 13. Check: 13 − 4 = 9 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Add 4 to both sides: n = 9 + 4 = ___.
The numbers were multiplied instead of combined with the inverse operation. Subtraction is undone by addition, so add 4 to both sides.
The subtraction ran in the wrong direction. Since 4 was taken away from n, n has to be larger than 9 — add 4 to both sides.
onLevel.explanationEs: Suma 4 en ambos lados: n = 9 + 4 = 13. Comprueba: 13 − 4 = 9 ✓
hints: This equation takes an amount away from n, and you need to find what n was before that happened.
Undo a subtraction with addition, applying it to both sides of the equation.
Add 4 to both sides. The left side becomes just n, and the right side becomes 9 + 4 — finish that addition.
hintsEs: Esta ecuación le quita una cantidad a n, y tienes que hallar cuánto valía n antes de eso.
Deshaz una resta con una suma, aplicándola a ambos lados de la ecuación.
Suma 4 en ambos lados. El lado izquierdo queda solo como n y el derecho queda como 9 + 4 — termina esa suma.

onLevel.stem: Unlock Card 3: A vault held some clue tokens. After the detective added 16 tokens, there were 50. The equation is t + 16 = 50. How many tokens were there before?
onLevel.explanation: Subtract 16 from both sides: t = 50 − 16 = 34. Check: 34 + 16 = 50 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 16 from both sides: t = 50 − 16 = ___.
That is the number of tokens the detective added, not how many were there before. Subtract 16 from both sides to find the starting amount.
The two numbers got multiplied. Since 16 was added to t, subtract 16 from both sides instead.
onLevel.stemEs: Tarjeta de desbloqueo 3: Una bóveda tenía algunas fichas de pistas. Después de que el detective agregó 16 fichas, había 50. La ecuación es t + 16 = 50. ¿Cuántas fichas había antes?
onLevel.explanationEs: Resta 16 en ambos lados: t = 50 − 16 = 34. Comprueba: 34 + 16 = 50 ✓
hints: Tokens were added to a starting amount to reach 50, so the starting amount has to be smaller than 50.
The equation t + 16 = 50 is undone by subtracting 16 from both sides.
Subtract 16 from both sides. The left side leaves just t, and the right side becomes 50 − 16 — finish that subtraction.
hintsEs: Se agregaron fichas a una cantidad inicial hasta llegar a 50, así que la cantidad inicial tiene que ser menor que 50.
La ecuación t + 16 = 50 se deshace restando 16 en ambos lados.
Resta 16 en ambos lados. El lado izquierdo deja solo a t y el derecho queda como 50 − 16 — termina esa resta.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — Crack the Detective's Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: To undo + 8 you SUBTRACT 8 from both sides, not add: x + 8 − 8 = 21 − 8, so x = 13. Check: 13 + 8 = 21 ✓
hints: Step 3 adds 8 to both sides. Does adding 8 again remove the + 8?
The inverse of adding 8 is subtracting 8. Subtract 8 from both sides to isolate x.
onLevel.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Descifra el error del detective
onLevel.explanation: The "Apply to both sides" step adds 8 again, which leaves x + 16 on the left instead of x alone. To undo + 8 you subtract 8 from both sides: x + 8 − 8 = 21 − 8, so x = 13. Checking, 13 + 8 = 21, while x = 29 would give 37.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Apply to both sides" vuelve a sumar 8, lo que deja x + 16 a la izquierda en lugar de x sola. Para deshacer + 8 restas 8 en ambos lados: x + 8 − 8 = 21 − 8, así que x = 13. Al comprobar, 13 + 8 = 21, mientras que x = 29 daría 37.

onLevel.title: Find the Equation Error
onLevel.correctWork: Inverse of subtraction is ADDITION. Add 18 to both sides: x = 45 + 18 = 63.
hints: Step 2 says the inverse of subtraction is subtraction. Is that right?
To undo −18, you need +18, not another −18. Addition undoes subtraction.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la ecuación
onLevel.explanation: The "Identify inverse" step claims subtraction undoes subtraction, which pushes the equation further from the answer instead of isolating x. Addition undoes subtraction, so add 18 to both sides of x − 18 = 45: x = 45 + 18 = 63. Checking, 63 − 18 = 45, while the answer 27 would give 9.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Identify inverse" afirma que la resta deshace la resta, lo que aleja la ecuación de la respuesta en lugar de despejar x. La suma deshace la resta, así que suma 18 en ambos lados de x − 18 = 45: x = 45 + 18 = 63. Al comprobar, 63 − 18 = 45, mientras que la respuesta 27 daría 9.

onLevel.prompt: A detective solved x + 25 = 60 and got x = 35. Another detective solved y − 25 = 60 and got y = 35. Are both correct? Explain using inverse operations and check each answer.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: For x + 25 = 60, the inverse operation is ___, so x = ___. Check: ___. For y − 25 = 60, the inverse operation is ___, so y = ___. Check: ___. Therefore, ___.
onLevel.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: The two equations use OPPOSITE operations (+25 and −25), so the same inverse step cannot work for both.
Solve each with its own inverse: subtract 25 for x + 25 = 60, but add 25 for y − 25 = 60. Then substitute each result back into its equation.
Start with x + 25 = 60: subtract 25 from both sides and compare with the detective's 35. Then add 25 for the y equation and see whether 35 survives that check.
onLevel.explanation: Only the first detective is right. For x + 25 = 60 the inverse is subtraction, so x = 60 − 25 = 35, and 35 + 25 = 60 checks out. For y − 25 = 60 the inverse is addition, so y = 60 + 25 = 85, not 35 — substituting 35 gives 35 − 25 = 10, not 60. Opposite operations need opposite inverses, even when the numbers look identical.
onLevel.explanationEs: Solo el primer detective tiene razón. Para x + 25 = 60 la inversa es la resta, así que x = 60 − 25 = 35, y 35 + 25 = 60 comprueba bien. Para y − 25 = 60 la inversa es la suma, así que y = 60 + 25 = 85, no 35: al sustituir 35 da 35 − 25 = 10, no 60. Operaciones opuestas necesitan inversas opuestas, aunque los números se vean idénticos.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake is applying the same operation instead of the inverse — for example, solving x − 7 = 15 by subtracting 7 from both sides (getting the wrong x = 8) instead of adding 7 to both sides (the correct x = 22). Another common mistake is doing the inverse operation to only one side, like solving x + 6 = 14 by subtracting 6 from the left but forgetting the right side. Before you submit, name the operation shown in the equation, choose its inverse, apply it to BOTH sides, and check by substituting your answer back into the original equation.

diagram.caption: The whole 12-mile trail (top bar) equals the distance walked (d) plus the 4.5 miles left; subtract 4.5 from 12 to find d = 7.5.

connect.scenario: A hiker has walked some distance and still has 4.5 miles left on a 12-mile trail. The equation d + 4.5 = 12 represents her situation, where d is the distance already walked.
connect.promptQuestion: How far has the hiker walked? How did you use inverse operations?
connect.prompt: The hiker walked ___ miles because d + 4.5 = 12 means d = 12 − ___ = ___.

check.explanation: Subtract 4.5 from both sides: d = 12 − 4.5 = 7.5 miles.
Addition and subtraction are inverse operations. Since 4.5 was added to d, subtract 4.5 to isolate d.

choices: Only if the trail is 11 miles

connect.modelAnswer: d + 4.5 = 12. Subtraction undoes addition, so subtract 4.5 from both sides: d = 12 − 4.5 = 7.5 miles walked. Check: 7.5 + 4.5 = 12. ✓

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Solve: p + 2.8 = 9.1
exitTicket.explanation: Subtract 2.8 from both sides: p = 9.1 − 2.8 = 6.3. Check: 6.3 + 2.8 = 9.1 ✓ (11.9 comes from adding instead of subtracting; 7.7 comes from subtracting each decimal place without regrouping — 9 − 2 = 7 and, without borrowing, 8 − 1 = 7; 3.25 comes from dividing 9.1 ÷ 2.8 instead of subtracting.)
choiceFeedback: You added 2.8 — undo it by subtracting from both sides.
Recheck your subtraction: 9.1 − 2.8 in the tenths place.
Subtract 2.8 from 9.1 — that's not the result.
hints: p has 2.8 added to it. To get p alone you must undo the addition — decimals follow the same rule as whole numbers.
Subtract 2.8 from both sides. Line up the decimal points and watch the tenths place for regrouping.
Set up 9.1 − 2.8: you can't take 8 tenths from 1 tenth, so borrow from the 9 first. Then check by adding 2.8 back to your result.
